target: Vi hittade en billigare lösning som fungerade lika bra.
english: We found a cheaper solution that worked just as well.
tip: Add -are to make comparatives: billig becomes billigare, cheaper.

target: Hon hittade till slut det förlorade passet i botten av sin väska.
english: She finally found the lost passport in the bottom of her bag.
tip: sin points back to the subject and means one's own: sin väska is her own bag, not someone else's.

english: The books are on the table.
tip: Swedish uses ligger for things resting flat: böckerna ligger på bordet, the books are on the table.

english: The Swedish right to roam is unique.
tip: Allemansrätten allows everyone to walk, camp, and pick berries on any land.

target: Hon frågade om vi hade ätit.
english: She asked if we had eaten.
tip: om means if or whether in an indirect question: hon frågade om vi hade ätit.

target: De smala gatorna i Gamla Stan.
english: The narrow streets in the Old Town.
tip: In the definite plural the adjective ends in -a and the noun in -na: de smala gatorna.

target: Hur du än gör blir det fel.
english: No matter what you do, it'll be wrong.
tip: än after a question word means no matter: hur du än gör, no matter what you do.
The definite article is a suffix, not a separate word: golv plus -et gives golvet, the floor.
Nouns ending in -el drop the e before the definite ending: himmel becomes himlen, not himmelen.
som means who, which or that for all genders and numbers, as in pojken som springer.
var is the past tense of vara (to be); the present is är, as in Dagen var lång.
Many adverbs are just the adjective plus -t: snabb (quick) becomes snabbt (quickly).
Swedish glues nouns into compounds: jul (Christmas) plus bord (table) makes julbord.
kläder (clothes) exists only in the plural, so it is always kläderna, never a singular form.
Definite phrases mark it twice, on the article and the noun ending, with the adjective taking -a: den starka vinden.
hem means toward home (movement); hemma means at home (location). Vägen hem is the way homeward.
gå igenom is a particle verb meaning to review or go through; igenom keeps the stress after the verb.
kom is the irregular past of komma (to come); the present is kommer, as in Jag kom från ett möte.
Many ett-words are identical in singular and plural: ett träd, flera träd; the definite plural adds -en, träden.
Many en-words take -ar in the plural, then add -na for the definite: en stol, stolar, stolarna.
The -s ending can be reciprocal: följas åt means to accompany each other, as in De följs åt.
hon (she) becomes henne as an object: jag ringer henne means I call her.

english: The night is short in summer.
tip: Seasons use på plus the definite form: på sommaren = in summer, på vintern = in winter.

english: We got a taste for it.
tip: få blod på tand literally means blood on the tooth; it means to get eager for more.

target: Vem som helst kan lära sig.
tip: Add som helst to a question word for any at all: vem som helst = anyone, vad som helst = anything.

target: Det kommer snart att vara vår.
tip: kommer att plus an infinitive is a future, often for predictions: det kommer att vara vår.

target: Vi tar en fika på kafét.
english: We'll have fika at the café.
tip: fika works as both noun and verb for a coffee-and-cake break: ta en fika = have a coffee break.

target: Vi sitter alla i samma båt.
english: We're all in the same boat.
tip: After samma the noun stays in its base form, no definite ending: samma båt, not samma båten.

target: Det var hon som hade rätt.
english: It was she who was right.
tip: Det var ... som is a cleft that highlights one part: Det var hon som hade rätt focuses on hon.

target: Stolen som står i hörnet är trasig.
english: The chair in the corner is broken.
tip: Swedish uses a posture verb where English says is: står (stands) for upright things, so stolen står i hörnet.
